saw_lines: Parents buy kids vitamins after a pediatrician says so, then reorder the same gummy every month without comparing.
So the sale is won in the first line, where a parent decides if a pediatrician claim is enough to click.
Your site shows 3155+ reviews and 1404+ reviews, yet 0 of 30 ads carry a proof number. Put the 3155 figure on the creative and open two ads with review quotes.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 27 Oct 2026
points: Your site shows 3155+ reviews, yet 0 of 30 live ads carry a proof number, so new parents have nothing to check. Put the 3155 figure on every creative and open two ads with a review quote.
Your site offers Subscribe & Save at up to 25% off, yet only 1 of 12 ads mention any offer. A buyer has no reason to act. Put Subscribe & Save in line one of three ads and on the creative.

7 of 12 copy ads open on the #1 pediatrician line, so other angles never get tested. Run three new openers from your products: Sleep Gummies at bedtime, the Protein Energy Waffle after school, and the growth gummy for ages 5+.

Your site shows $40, yet 0 of 30 live ads mention price, so a buyer meets no number before the click. Lead one ad with the price per month and what that covers, then run it against your strongest hook.

ads_1: New paid openers for Sleep Gummies at bedtime and the Protein Waffle after school
